name: ProtocolQA Open-Ended
intro: ProtocolQA Open-Ended是OpenAI在o1系统卡中披露的内部开放式湿实验故障排除评测。系统卡仅说明把108道FutureHouse ProtocolQA多项选择题改为开放式简答，题目包含常见已发表实验方案中的严重错误、执行后的湿实验结果，并询问如何修复流程；选题与改写细节、评分器、数据发布和许可均未披露。
build_method: 将108道FutureHouse ProtocolQA多项选择题改为开放式湿实验故障排除简答题；系统卡未披露子集选择规则或精确改写流程
task_type: 开放式问答, 生物安全评测
eval_feature: 开放式简答pass@1，并与19名具有一年以上湿实验经验的博士科学家比较；评分器与计分实现未披露
scale: 内部108道开放式简答题；未披露数据集载荷、划分或发布
build_method_en: Modify 108 FutureHouse ProtocolQA multiple-choice questions into open-ended short-answer wet-lab troubleshooting tasks; the system card does not disclose subset-selection rules or the exact rewrite procedure
eval_feature_en: Open-ended short-answer pass@1 and comparison with 19 PhD scientists who each have more than one year of wet-lab experience; grader and scoring implementation are not disclosed
intro_en: ProtocolQA Open-Ended is an internal open-ended wet-lab troubleshooting evaluation disclosed in OpenAI's o1 System Card. The card only says that 108 FutureHouse ProtocolQA MCQs are modified into open-ended short-answer tasks containing egregious errors in common published protocols, the wet-lab result, and a request for how to fix the procedure. Selection, rewrite, grading, release, and licensing details are not disclosed.
scale_en: 108 internal open-ended short-answer questions; dataset payload, splits, and release are not disclosed

drawio_review_note: reviewed_at=2026-07-18; source_stage=official-system-card alignment; scope=ProtocolQA Open-Ended only. This benchmark has no standalone paper or public release identified by the reviewed source. The fixed primary evidence is OpenAI's December 5, 2024 o1 System Card at https://openai.com/index/openai-o1-system-card/ and the versioned PDF https://cdn.openai.com/o1-system-card-20241205.pdf. The reviewed PDF SHA256 is 3ba7bdbe69e022f6be0527edbfe18ac1becdea48d5be9891ab764ff336c8a033. The graph is limited to Section 5.5.6. That section states that OpenAI modifies 108 multiple-choice questions from FutureHouse's ProtocolQA dataset into open-ended short-answer questions, making the evaluation harder and more realistic than the multiple-choice version. The questions introduce egregious errors in common published protocols, describe the wet-lab result of carrying out the protocol, and ask how to fix the procedure. The system card does not say that all 135 original ProtocolQA items were considered, does not identify which 108 were used, and does not specify whether the public 108 items in the LAB-Bench repository are identical to this internal 108-item set. The diagram therefore does not infer an identity join from the matching count. OpenAI performs new expert baselining with 19 PhD scientists who have more than one year of wet-lab experience. The system-card chart reports pass@1 values of GPT-4o 16%, o1-preview 24%, o1 pre-mitigation 22%, and o1 post-mitigation 24%. The text says all models underperform both the consensus expert baseline of 57% and the median expert baseline of 42%. These values are recorded as system-card results, not as a reconstructed executable run. The metric name pass@1 is a disclosed chart label only and is not evidence that exactly one response was sampled per item. The actual sampling count, retry policy, and scoring implementation are not disclosed. Reproducibility limits are explicit: selection rules, rewrite procedure, grader and scoring implementation, dataset release, and license are not disclosed. The card also does not disclose item IDs, item schema, answer keys, reference-answer format, annotator assignment, expert-response aggregation, adjudication, prompt text, model generation settings, checkpoint identifiers beyond the chart labels, retry policy, per-item pass labels, split design, or a downloadable evaluation harness. No public repository, dataset URL, Git commit, data revision, or item-file hash is fabricated to fill those gaps. The PDF hash pins the evidence that actually exists. The evaluation is not the LAB-Bench paper's separate 20-item open-answer audit. That LAB-Bench audit rewrites 20 ProtocolQA questions where needed, evaluates Claude 3.5 Sonnet and GPT-4o, grades against the ideal multiple-choice answer with an expert biologist paper author, and uses a second reviewer. ProtocolQA Open-Ended instead appears in the OpenAI system card as a 108-item evaluation with different reported model labels and a new 19-scientist baseline. The two workflows remain separate in labels, topology, review prose, and release claims. Solid arrows show only the disclosed 108-MCQ source, conversion to open-ended short answer, egregious protocol error, wet-lab result, repair question, model pass@1 branch, expert branch, and comparison. Dashed arrows mark the fixed system-card source, undisclosed selection and rewrite details, undisclosed grader and scoring implementation, undisclosed dataset release and license, and the non-equivalence of the LAB-Bench 20-item audit. English and Chinese specs have identical semantic node IDs, types, positions, edge types, styles, waypoints, and modules. Every secondary edge explicitly sets dashed=true; no edge carries a label. Source-stage fallback fields remain null or empty. Formal Draw.io, architecture JSON, SVG, PNG, catalog, manifest, and synchronization files are intentionally unchanged in this source-stage handoff.
